prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins that inhibitors cannot reach

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the strongest case on the table because a single physical-chemical principle, induced proximity, is demonstrated in two independent molecular forms. Bifunctional PROTACs (2001) and thalidomide-type molecular glues act through the same logic: a small molecule forms a ternary complex that brings a ligase to a protein it would not otherwise ubiquitinate, so the target is removed catalytically, not occupied stoichiometrically. That moves pharmacology from occupancy-driven to event-driven, and it is a genuinely new capability that reaches targets inhibitors cannot. It is quantitative (cooperativity, ternary-complex structure, degradation kinetics), independently confirmed by many groups and ligases, and it can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence. Opening support is also the broadest on the shortlist: three first places, six top-three rankings, ranked by all eight members. Crews and Deshaies stand for the concept and first demonstrations; Handa stands for the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target, which showed that glues are the same principle found in an existing drug and gives the prize its second pillar.
statement.case_against: The candidate is compound. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work, Sakamoto and Kim as co-authors of the founding 2001 PROTAC paper, Ito alongside Handa, and Gray's work on degrader chemistry are all excluded by a three-name cut, and the committee must accept that. Clinical proof is the second weakness: glue-class drugs are approved but heterobifunctional degraders have not yet shown an approved benefit, so a PROTAC-centred citation could look early. A citation that spans both PROTACs and glues also risks being too broad to be tied to a precise discovery, and a narrower PROTAC-only citation risks ignoring the glue mechanism that many members regard as separate.

responses.point: Aili would honour the PROTAC core with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, accept that glue degraders are partly left out, and regards recognition as timely given two decades of independent confirmation.
responses.response: I agree on timing and on Crews and Deshaies, but I do not think leaving glues out is neutral. The cereblon-thalidomide mechanism is what showed that induced proximity works in an approved drug, which answers the clinical-maturity worry we both have about PROTACs. Handa gives us a discovery with a clear date and a clear mechanism, whereas Ciulli's contribution is real but largely about optimising VHL-based design after the concept existed. I would ask Daniel what exactly Ciulli discovered that was not already implied by Crews and Deshaies, and I am willing to be persuaded if the structural cooperativity work is seen as foundational.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first, defends Liu with Komor and Gaudelli as the natural unit, and puts PROTACs second while accepting that glues are a separate discovery with its own claim.
responses.response: I take the chemical point that base editing is a deaminase reaction on a Cas-bound single-stranded window and that it is clean and mature. My reservation is the one Andrei himself half raises: this is an application of a genome-targeting platform that this committee already recognised in 2020, and trainee credit (Komor, Gaudelli) versus the parallel Nishida-Kondo editor makes a defensible citation harder than for degradation. I disagree that the glue branch is only a complication; I read it as half of the discovery. I would keep base editing as the strongest alternative, and would favour a Liu-alone configuration over three names if we went there.

responses.point: Zou ranks degradation first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, treating the PROTAC concept and the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism as two distinct pillars, with Ciulli's work also decisive.
responses.response: This is closest to my own configuration, and I am glad to see the structural grounding stressed. Where I would push Xiaodong is on whether two pillars can really share one citation. I think they can, if the citation states the principle (recruiting the ubiquitin-proteasome system by a small molecule) and not the compound class, but the committee should test that wording before committing, and I want her view on whether the ternary-complex structural work is enough to justify Ciulli over Handa.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling first, arguing that Buchwald and Hartwig changed how chemists build bonds everywhere, that recognition is overdue, and that two laureates make a clean configuration.
responses.response: I accept that Buchwald-Hartwig amination is mature, mechanistically well understood and used constantly, and the attribution is cleaner than in degradation. My difficulty is the cross-coupling prize of 2010: the question I would put to Peter is what new capability this adds beyond a very good extension of the same catalytic principle. If the committee judges ligand-controlled C-N coupling a distinct achievement, it is a serious candidate and the strongest synthetic one here, but I do not see it opening something previously unforeseen in the way degradation or base editing do.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics first as an unambiguous, four-decade-old origin with a clean two-person attribution and clear game-changing impact on simulation.
responses.response: Johan makes the strongest attribution argument on the table, and I cannot fault the scientific standing of the 1985 paper. I do not see it displaced by degradation on merit. Where I differ is on how the committee should weigh it: only one of eight openings ranked it first and it did not reach the top three of any other member, so it lacks the cross-disciplinary support to win a majority in this discussion. I would like to hear which discoveries beyond the method itself he thinks the committee could cite, since a method citation is harder to explain than a molecular principle.

uncertainties: Whether a single citation can credibly cover both PROTACs and molecular glues, or whether the committee should choose one lineage.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies, and how Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are acknowledged.
Whether the lack of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes the PROTAC arm premature.
Whether base editing is seen as a distinct chemical invention given the 2020 prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the preferred configuration. I have no stated connection to Crews, Deshaies or Handa. I note that I am a nanophysicist, that nanopore sequencing (B048) is close to my own device interests, and that Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr sit on the committee, but none of these touches B014.
